name: Mozambique

findings.summary: State operator Tmcel signed a US$23 million deal with Huawei to extend 4G coverage nationwide, starting in Maputo and Matola, while testing 5G in the capital.
findings.analyst_inference: RAN expansion; core vendor not stated. The 2022 Telecom Review item frames the same US$23m contract as supporting 5G deployment with Huawei expertise. Value relayed by trade press, not a filing, so left out of value fields. Tmcel also signed a separate five-year network/mobile-money deal with Ericsson (per the BuddeComm digest), so Tmcel is not single-vendor. Vodacom Mozambique (5G launched May 2023) and Movitel (Viettel, Vietnam) RAN vendors were not identified.

findings.local_actor: Presidency military household (Casa Militar); Maputo and Matola
findings.summary: A China Eximbank-financed National Command Information Network, implemented by ZTE, covered 450 CCTV cameras in Maputo and Matola and a Presidential Guard monitoring centre for intercepting phone, SMS and internet traffic.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: AidData records a loan of about US$149.5m ratified December 2014, with ZTE as contractor, and says it reached implementation but completion is unclear; coded tier 4 (financing closed, implementation started), not 5. Global Voices says a firm owned by former President Guebuza's son held the contract and subcontracted ZTE. Pre-2020 and still_current not confirmed. Loan value comes from a research dataset, not a filing, so left out of value fields. Interception component makes this a surveillance capability, not just traffic CCTV.

findings.controller: Government of Mozambique (national e-government data centre)
findings.summary: A China Eximbank concessional loan of RMB 230 million signed in 2012 funded a national data centre and shared e-government infrastructure built by Huawei; AidData records the data centre as completed in December 2015.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is the state, so pole is domestic with Huawei as builder; if Huawei IT equipment or ongoing Huawei support is documented, the IT layer would be prc. AidData converts the loan to about US$35m at signing; not entered as a value. Which facility this is (possibly among the government data centres the US trade.gov guide lists, e.g. Maluana) and whether still in service is unconfirmed. Single source.

findings.summary: Raxio Group opened its first carrier-neutral colocation data centre in Mozambique in May 2024, part of a US$290 million multi-country African build-out financed by equity and Proparco/EAIF debt.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: Raxio is backed by US private-equity firm Roha Group and French fund Meridiam, and its controlling home jurisdiction was not established in this pass. Mozambique-specific capacity and cost not stated; the US$290m covers seven markets, so no value entered. Opening reported but operational scale unconfirmed; tier 5 is a cautious reading of a live facility. Only one source opened. Audit 2026-10-28: Data Centre Review (2024-05-29) confirms the MZ1 opening at Beluluane near Maputo; the US$290m build-out and Proparco/EAIF financing were not on pages read.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Interior / police (PRM); Maputo and Nampula
findings.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers ratified an US$88.7 million Korea Eximbank loan for a public-security project: CCTV, fingerprint identification, a Maputo central operations room and regional rooms in Nampula province, running to end-2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null because the equipment vendor (the controller under SPEC v0.2) is not named; Korean financing suggests but does not establish a Korean supplier, which would make it third. Loan value relayed by press, not a filing, so left out of value fields. Delivery status after 2021 unknown. Single opened source.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or export-licence reporting surfaced in searches on AI and data-centre activity; not searched separately

models.null_reason: one search found a draft national AI strategy (UNESCO-supported) and a new AI association, but no government frontier-model partnership or sovereign model

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power project surfaced; budget spent on networks, facilities and applications

research_gaps: Which vendors supply Vodacom Mozambique's 5G RAN/core (launched May 2023) and Movitel's (Viettel) RAN/core?
Did Tmcel's US$200m 2020 modernisation financing come from China Eximbank (reported by @Verdade, unconfirmed) and which vendor did it fund?
Was the ZTE National Command Information Network (450 cameras plus Casa Militar interception centre) completed, and is it still in use?
Which firm supplies the Korea Eximbank-financed public-security CCTV/AFIS project (2021-2025), and was it delivered?
Is the 2015 Huawei-built e-government data centre the Maluana facility, and does Huawei still supply or support its IT equipment?
Raxio Group's controlling shareholder and home jurisdiction, and Raxio Mozambique capacity.
Does the final national AI strategy (draft mid-2026) name foreign AI or cloud partners? Any vendor of the 2Africa landing or other cables (HMN Tech involvement)?
